title: End-to-end onboarding pipeline for open LLMs: weights intake to profile publishing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build a repeatable, auditable pipeline that takes a new open-source LLM from raw weights to a Redwood-managed catalog entry with pinned versions and a published performance profile. The pipeline must: (1) ingest model weights and metadata with provenance and license checks; (2) run automatic conversion to our optimized formats (float16/quantized artifacts) and produce SBOM-like artifact metadata; (3) validate functional parity (sanity prompts, tokenization checks), safety baseline (toxicity/sensitive prompt runs), and performance benchmarking across representative hardware/sequence-lengths; (4) auto-generate model-version entries in the model catalog with version pin, performance profile, recommended quantization settings, and CI gating; (5) surface artifacts and results in Console and publish a performance snapshot to the public model catalog page.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline accepts weights (S3/URL/registry) and verifies license + checksum before any conversion
Automated conversion produces deterministic artifacts (float16 + two quantized variants) and uploads to artifacts store with provenance metadata
Validation suite runs: tokenizer parity, 100 curated sanity prompts, 5 safety checks, and end-to-end generation regression compared to baseline outputs with configurable thresholds
Performance profile produced includes latency P50/P95 for short (16), medium (128), long (1024) sequences on supported instance types and memory/throughput targets
Catalog entry created with pinned version, stable identifier, recommended quantization profile, and link to artifact SBOM
CI gate fails onboarding if performance regressions exceed thresholds or if license is incompatible
Results and artifacts are displayed in Console (Model -> Versions -> <version> -> Profile) and a summary JSON published to the public model catalog API
pipeline_steps: Weights intake: ingest URL/S3/registry, verify checksum, capture origin and license, quarantine copy for conversion
Static checks: license compatibility, file-level malware scan, and basic architecture detection (decoder/encoder/mix)
Conversion: run conversion container to produce standard Redwood formats + quantized variants (q4f32, q5b), emit deterministic metadata
Unit validation: tokenizer sanity tests, shape checks, KV-cache integration smoke tests
Functional validation: run curated prompt set, compute per-prompt diffs vs baseline or golden outputs
Safety baseline: run sensitive prompts and toxicity classifiers, flag if above thresholds
Perf benchmarking: automated runs on matrix of instance types (A100, H100, T4) and sequence lengths with profiler traces
Profile generation: synthesize latency/cost/throughput recommendations and quantization guidance
Catalog publish: create version entry, pin model to artifact IDs, annotate with release and security flags
Post-publish: notify PM/RESEARCH for manual spot-checks and schedule regular re-evals
test_plan: Unit tests for conversion containers and artifact metadata generation
Integration tests covering full pipeline on a small toy model (2-layer transformer) in staging
End-to-end QA run for three candidate open models (small, medium, large) against performance SLOs
Chaos test: intentional corrupted weights to ensure intake rejects malformed artifacts
Security smoke: license mismatch and KMS access boundary tests
Canary publish: only create catalog draft unless human approval flips auto-publish flag (for first 2 weeks)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Upstream license ambiguity could expose Redwood. Mitigation: require SPDX-like field and manual legal review if ambiguous
Risk: Conversion non-determinism leads to flaky validation. Mitigation: pin conversion container image, add artifact checksums and deterministic seeds
Risk: Perf benchmarking noise across infra shapes. Mitigation: use multiple runs + trimmed mean, store full traces for post-hoc analysis
Risk: Long-running conversion/backfill consumes infra. Mitigation: quota conversions per org, prioritize by customer demand and set cost caps
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable pipeline for internal research models only, produce draft catalog entries (no public publish)
Phase 2 (limited public): allow select open models with PM sign-off to be published to public catalog, enable console visibility for customers
Phase 3 (GA): pipeline runs for all supported open models, CI gating enforced, automated publishing enabled
Fallback: if perf profile shows unexpected regressions post-publish, automatically flag version as deprecated and route live traffic to fallback model variants
comments: 2025-11-05 - Kickoff: scoping session with PM (Lydia Park) and Research (Diego Ramos). Decided to prioritize deterministic conversion and provenance metadata over supporting every quantization scheme initially.

2025-12-12 - Design review: agreed on artifact metadata schema (artifact_id, parent_weights_url, spdx_license, conversion_container_sha). Action: Rajat to prototype conversion container and metadata schema.

2026-01-20 - Prototype complete: conversion container produces float16 + q4f32 artifacts. Early perf runs show 8-12% latency variance on H100 across runs. Added trimmed-mean to benchmark harness (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pulls/21).
2026-02-15 - Security review kickoff: Security requested SBOM and license auto-blocking for GPL-like licenses; legal to onboard manual review flow. Ticket added to legal queue.
2026-03-01 - QA: First full staging run on 'citrine-7b' completed. Tokenizer parity failures (3/100 prompts) traced to tokenizer version mismatch; added tokenizer-version pinning step and re-ran.
2026-03-10 - Code review: console UI shim to show profiling snapshot merged (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/998). Pending: add link to artifact SBOM and per-run profiler traces.

2026-03-14 - Current: pipeline smoke passing in staging for two models. Remaining: finalize legal review flow, add CI gating that blocks publish if safety tests fail, and create automation for version pin rollbacks. Assigned to Rajat for next sprint.
